# Alignment Control Align and distribute the selected layers from a compact button row, or place them in their frame with a 3×3 grid. One layer aligns to its frame, several to each other. ## Release Version: 0.2.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT. ## Prerequisites Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package. React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported. ## Install Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version: ~~~sh npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/alignment-control/0.2.0.json ~~~ For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs. ## Files and dependencies - @ui/alignment-control-geometry.ts - @ui/alignment-control-grid.tsx - @ui/alignment-control-state.tsx - @ui/alignment-control-toolbar.tsx - @ui/alignment-control.tsx - @ui/alignment-control.md Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0. Pinned registry dependencies: none. ## Installed guide This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as alignment-control.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates. ## Minimal working example This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence. ~~~tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { AlignmentGrid, type AlignmentPosition } from "@/components/ui/alignment-control"; export default function AlignmentControlExample() { const [position, setPosition] = useState({ x: "center", y: "center" }); return (
{position.x} / {position.y}
); } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | selectionCount | number | | How many layers are selected. Align needs one, distribute needs three; buttons that need more stay focusable and say why. | | onAlign | (action, { target }) => void | | Called with the action and what it aligns to: "parent" for one layer, "selection" for several. Your app moves the layers. | | shortcuts | Partial> | | Shortcut text for each action's tooltip, such as "Alt+A". Your app binds the keys. | | disabled / motion / messages | boolean / object | | Turn the control off, turn off tooltip transitions, or replace its text, for example to translate it. | | AlignmentControlGroup / Button / Icon | parts | | Boxed sets of buttons, one action each, and the action icons for your own menus. | | AlignmentGrid value / onValueChange | { x, y } \| null | | Where the layers sit in their frame, as start, center or end on each axis; null when they differ or sit between positions. | | AlignmentGrid tooltips | boolean | true | Name each cell on hover, such as Top left, as the toolbar's buttons do. motion turns off the tooltip's transition. | | alignRects / positionRect / positionOf | helpers | | Optional geometry for your canvas: apply an action to rects, move a rect to a grid position, or read its position. | ## Supported states - mixed - disabled ## Customization Use the button row to dispatch object alignment commands. The host applies them in its own coordinate space using the parent frame or selected bounds as indicated by the callback. Use the grid to capture a 3×3 placement value. Both can be styled independently, and geometry helpers are available for rectangular bounds. ~~~tsx ~~~ Keep accessible names on icon-only actions. Verify the target with one and several selected objects, and verify that distribution is unavailable below three. ## Accessibility and integration checks - The buttons form one toolbar: Tab reaches it once, and the arrow keys, Home and End move between buttons. - Each button is named by its action, with its shortcut exposed, and its tooltip says when more layers are needed. - The grid is a radio group of nine named positions; arrow keys move across and down and apply the position. Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling. ## Updates and conflicts Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/alignment-control/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates. If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry. ## License MIT. Dependencies retain their respective licenses.

items.title: Animation Timeline
items.description: Arrange clips and keyframes on tracks, with a ruler and playhead.

files.content:
# Animation Timeline

Arrange when things animate with clips and keyframes on tracks. Drag, resize and snap them, scrub the ruler, and let your app run playback. Each edit commits once.

## Release

Version: 0.1.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/animation-timeline/0.1.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/animation-timeline-drag.ts

- @ui/animation-timeline-items.tsx

- @ui/animation-timeline-math.ts

- @ui/animation-timeline-root.tsx

- @ui/animation-timeline-state.tsx

- @ui/animation-timeline-toolbar.tsx

- @ui/animation-timeline-tracks.tsx

- @ui/animation-timeline-view.ts

- @ui/animation-timeline.tsx

- @ui/animation-timeline.md

Npm dependencies: none beyond the host React/shadcn setup.

Pinned registry dependencies: context-menu@0.1.2, inspector-field@0.2.0, playback-controls@0.1.0.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as animation-timeline.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { AnimationTimeline, type TimelineItem } from "@/components/ui/animation-timeline";

const tracks = [{ id: "title", label: "Title" }];

export default function AnimationTimelineExample() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<TimelineItem[]>([{ id: "enter", kind: "clip", trackId: "title", label: "Enter", start: 0, duration: 1.5 }]);
  const [selection, setSelection] = useState<string[]>([]);
  const [time, setTime] = useState(0);
  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);
  return (
    <AnimationTimeline className="rounded-xl border border-border p-3" label="Title animation"
      tracks={tracks} items={items} duration={4} selection={selection} onSelectionChange={setSelection}
      onItemsCommit={setItems} currentTime={time} onSeek={setTime} onSeekCommit={setTime}
      playing={playing} onPlayingChange={setPlaying} />
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| tracks | { id, label, hidden?, locked? }[] |  | Rows from top to bottom. Your app owns them. |
| items | TimelineItem[] |  | Clips with start and duration, and keyframes with time. Each names its trackId. |
| duration | number |  | The timeline's length in seconds. |
| selection / onSelectionChange | string[] / function |  | Selected item ids. Your app owns them. |
| onItemsCommit | (items, detail) => void |  | Called once per finished drag or key press. detail names the action and ids. |
| onItemsChange | (items, detail) => void |  | Live items while dragging, and the starting items when a drag is cancelled. |
| currentTime / onSeek / onSeekCommit | number / functions |  | The playhead in seconds, live moves and finished moves. |
| playing / onPlayingChange | boolean / function |  | Playback state. Your app runs playback. |
| loop / onLoopChange | boolean / function |  | Passing loop shows the Loop button. |
| onTrackHiddenChange / onTrackLockedChange | functions |  | Each shows that action for every track. |
| onDuplicate / onDelete | (ids) => void |  | Each adds its action to the item menu. Your app changes the items. |
| step / largeStep | number | 0.1 / 1 | Seconds moved by arrow keys, and with Shift. |
| minClipDuration | number | 0.1 | The shortest a clip can be, in seconds. |
| snap | boolean | true | Snap to the playhead, item edges and ruler ticks. Hold Alt while dragging to turn it off. |
| defaultZoom | "fit" \| number | "fit" | The starting zoom. Fit shows the whole timeline; a percent zooms in from it and scrolls sideways. |
| zoomLevels | number[] | [150, 200, 300, 400] | Zoomed-in choices after Fit, in percent of Fit. |
| pixelsPerSecond / maxZoom | number | 80 / 800 | The scale until the space is measured, and the limit for Ctrl or Cmd + scroll. |
| formatTime / container / disabled / messages | function / HTMLElement / boolean / object |  | Replace the time format, choose where menus portal, turn off editing, replace the text. |
| AnimationTimelineToolbar / Zoom / Body / Ruler / Item | parts |  | Compose your own toolbar or arrangement. |
| useAnimationTimeline | hook |  | Live items, time and scale, for custom parts. |

## Supported states

- empty

- locked

- disabled

## Integration

Give each track and timeline item an id. Each clip has a starting time and duration, while each keyframe has a time. Supply a duration in seconds and keep selection and items in the host.

Route onItemsChange to live preview and onItemsCommit to a single history entry. Update currentTime from your host clock or media player and wire onSeekCommit to its seek operation.

## Customization

Style the root for a docked timeline and compose AnimationTimelineToolbar, AnimationTimelineBody and the row parts for custom arrangements. Set zoomLevels to values that suit the host duration.

```tsx
<AnimationTimelineToolbar className="border-b border-border bg-muted p-2" />
```

## Accessibility and integration checks

- Each clip and keyframe is a labelled button that says its track and time, and Enter or Space selects it.

- Arrow keys move the selection through time and between tracks, and Shift moves further. Each press commits once.

- Alt with Left or Right changes a clip's end; adding Shift changes its start.

- Delete and Ctrl or Cmd + D run those actions, and the menu key opens the item menu.

- The ruler is a slider for the playhead. Escape cancels a drag.

- On touch, a short hold starts a drag, so scrolling never moves a clip.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/animation-timeline/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates.

If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry.

## License

MIT. Dependencies retain their respective licenses.

files.content:
# Browser Bar

Browser controls for web previews and embedded pages: back, forward, reload, an address field and an action button. It adapts as it narrows, then floats.

## Release

Version: 0.1.1. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/browser-bar/0.1.1.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/browser-bar-parts.tsx

- @ui/browser-bar-root.tsx

- @ui/browser-bar.tsx

- @ui/browser-bar.md

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: none.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as browser-bar.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { BrowserBar, BrowserBarAddress, BrowserBarBack } from "@/components/ui/browser-bar";

export default function BrowserBarExample() {
  const home = "https://example.com";
  const [url, setUrl] = useState(home);
  return (
    <BrowserBar className="rounded-xl border border-border p-2">
      <BrowserBarBack disabled={url === home} onClick={() => setUrl(home)} />
      <BrowserBarAddress value={url} onValueCommit={setUrl} />
    </BrowserBar>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| variant | "standalone" \| "attached" | "standalone" | A complete rounded bar, or one that joins the top of the content below it. Below 240px either becomes a floating bar. |
| disabled / motion / container / messages | boolean / HTMLElement / object |  | Turn off every control; turn off transitions; portal tooltips elsewhere; replace the text. |
| BrowserBarBack / Forward / Reload | parts |  | Named icon buttons with tooltips. Your app handles each click and disables what is unavailable. |
| BrowserBarButton | part |  | Your own icon button, with a label, icon and optional shortcut. |
| BrowserBarAddress value / onValueCommit | string / (address) => void |  | The current address. Enter commits a changed address; Escape or leaving the field restores it. |
| BrowserBarAction active | boolean | false | A filled button such as Run and Stop. active shows it as on. A narrow bar shows only its icon and keeps its name for screen readers. |
| --browser-stroke | CSS variable |  | The outline colour, for matching a selected frame or your own surface. |

## Supported states

- disabled

## Integration

Compose the address field with the navigation and action buttons your host supports. The bar calls your callbacks. Connect them to your own history, reload, and run controls.

One tap focuses the native address field. On touch browsers the keyboard uses the URL layout and Go commits the address. Keep the committed address in host state. Validate and normalize submitted URLs before navigating, and keep navigation controls disabled when there is nowhere to go.

## Customization

Give the root a rounded border for a card header. Use className on BrowserBarAddress for a quieter address field and the action icon slot for a host-specific action.

```tsx
<BrowserBarAddress className="rounded-full bg-muted" value={url} onValueCommit={setUrl} />
```

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The bar is a named group of labelled controls, each with a tooltip.

- Escape in the address field restores the current address and leaves the field.

"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { BrowserBar, BrowserBarAddress, BrowserBarBack } from "@/components/ui/browser-bar";

export default function BrowserBarExample() {
  const home = "https://example.com";
  const [url, setUrl] = useState(home);

      <BrowserBarBack disabled={url === home} onClick={() => setUrl(home)} />
      <BrowserBarAddress value={url} onValueCommit={setUrl} />

|---|---|---|---|

# Canvas Toolbar

A toolbar for any design tool. Pointer and Hand come ready to use, with room for your own tools and actions, shortcut tooltips, and horizontal or vertical layouts.

## Release

Version: 0.1.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/canvas-toolbar/0.1.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/canvas-toolbar-items.tsx

- @ui/canvas-toolbar-root.tsx

- @ui/canvas-toolbar-state.tsx

- @ui/canvas-toolbar.tsx

## Installed guide

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { CanvasToolbar, CanvasToolbarHand, CanvasToolbarPointer, CanvasToolbarTools } from "@/components/ui/canvas-toolbar";

export default function CanvasToolbarExample() {
  const [tool, setTool] = useState<string | null>("pointer");
  return (
    <CanvasToolbar className="w-fit rounded-full border border-border p-2">
      <CanvasToolbarTools value={tool} onValueChange={setTool} shortcuts>
        <CanvasToolbarPointer />
        <CanvasToolbarHand />
      </CanvasToolbarTools>
    </CanvasToolbar>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| orientation | "horizontal" \| "vertical" | "horizontal" | A row for a dock, or a column for a rail. Arrow keys and tooltips follow it. |
| variant | "floating" \| "plain" | "floating" | A raised box in either orientation, or no box when the toolbar sits inside your own container. |
| disabled / motion / container / messages | boolean / HTMLElement / object |  | Turn off every item; turn off transitions; portal tooltips elsewhere; replace the text. |
| CanvasToolbarTools value / onValueChange | string \| null |  | The chosen tool, which your app owns. Pair "hand" with Canvas Viewport's panning. |
| CanvasToolbarTools deselectable | boolean | false | Choosing the current tool again turns it off and reports null. |
| CanvasToolbarTools shortcuts | boolean | false | Listens for each tool's single-key shortcut while nobody is typing. |
| CanvasToolbarPointer / CanvasToolbarHand | parts |  | The standard tools, with their names, icons and V and H shortcuts. Any prop can be replaced. |
| CanvasToolbarTool | part |  | Your own tool: value, label, icon and shortcut. showLabel puts the name beside the icon. |
| CanvasToolbarButton | part |  | An action, or a toggle with pressed. It works as a menu trigger. |
| disabled / reason | boolean / string |  | On a tool or button: it stays focusable, and the reason replaces its tooltip. |
| CanvasToolbarSeparator / CanvasToolbarTip | parts |  | A line between sets of items, and the tooltip for your own controls. |

## Supported states

- disabled

## Integration

Wrap mutually exclusive tools in CanvasToolbarTools. Use CanvasToolbarButton for actions that run once and CanvasToolbarSeparator to group them. Supply a custom icon and label to CanvasToolbarTool.

Keep the selected tool in the host and let canvas gestures read it. Enable shortcuts when the toolbar owns the relevant keys, and scope multiple toolbars so the same shortcut does not activate competing controls.

## Customization

Use a rounded border for an inset pill or make the root full width with justify-start for a docked toolbar. Pass className to individual tools when they need different widths.

```tsx
<CanvasToolbar className="w-full justify-start border-b border-border bg-background" />
```

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The toolbar is one tab stop. Arrow keys, Home and End move between items, following its orientation.

- Tools form a radio group, so the chosen tool is announced. Enter or Space chooses the focused tool.

- Icon-only items are named, and a disabled item's reason is read as its description.

- Single-key shortcuts are opt-in and never fire while typing or with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt held.

- The hover box does not slide with reduced motion.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

# Color Picker

Edit a colour from a compact row: its swatch opens a picker with an area, hue and opacity sliders, Hex, RGB or HSL entry with opacity, an eyedropper and swatches.

## Release

Version: 0.2.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/color-picker/0.2.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/color-picker-color.ts

- @ui/color-picker-content.tsx

- @ui/color-picker-inputs.tsx

- @ui/color-picker-root.tsx

- @ui/color-picker-state.tsx

- @ui/color-picker.tsx

- @ui/color-picker.md

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: none.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as color-picker.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  ColorPicker, ColorPickerArea, ColorPickerContent, ColorPickerError, ColorPickerField, ColorPickerFormatSwitch,
  ColorPickerHexInput, ColorPickerLabel, ColorPickerSlider, ColorPickerSwatches, ColorPickerTrigger, ColorPickerValue, type ColorValue,
} from "@/components/ui/color-picker";

export default function ColorPickerExample() {
  const [fill, setFill] = useState<ColorValue>({ hex: "#5684ff", alpha: 1 });
  return (
    <ColorPicker label="Fill" value={fill} onValueCommit={setFill}>
      <ColorPickerField><ColorPickerLabel /><ColorPickerHexInput /><ColorPickerTrigger /></ColorPickerField>
      <ColorPickerError />
      <ColorPickerContent>
        <ColorPickerFormatSwitch />
        <ColorPickerValue />
        <ColorPickerArea />
        <ColorPickerSlider channel="hue" />
        <ColorPickerSlider channel="alpha" />
        <ColorPickerSwatches />
      </ColorPickerContent>
    </ColorPicker>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| value | { hex, alpha } \| null |  | The committed colour, as six-digit hex and opacity from 0 to 1; null when a selection holds different colours. |
| onValueCommit | (value) => void |  | Called once per finished change: a released drag, a typed value, a swatch or the eyedropper. |
| onValueChange | (value) => void |  | Live values while dragging the area or a slider, for previewing on your canvas. |
| label | string |  | Names the colour, such as Fill. Labels the swatch, inputs and picker. |
| swatches | (string \| { hex, alpha })[] |  | Colours your app offers, such as the document's colours. |
| recent / onRecentChange / recentLimit | { hex, alpha }[] |  | The last colours chosen, newest first. Pass recent and onRecentChange to store them; otherwise the picker keeps them. |
| format / defaultFormat / onFormatChange | "hex" \| "rgb" \| "hsl" | "hex" | The format the picker's inputs show. Your app always receives hex and opacity. |
| disabled / readOnly / motion / container | boolean / HTMLElement |  | Turn off editing or opening; turn off transitions; portal the picker elsewhere. |
| ColorPickerContent side / align | "bottom" \| "top" \| "left" \| "right" | "bottom" | Where the picker opens against the row. It flips, then moves to the other axis, rather than cover the row. |
| ColorPickerContent anchor | Element |  | What the picker opens beside. Defaults to the row; when the row is laid out as contents, such as in an inspector's columns, the nearest box around it. |
| ColorPickerField / Label | parts |  | The field's box and the colour's name. Put the label inside the field or before it; pressing anywhere in the field except the swatch selects the hex value. |
| ColorPickerAlphaInput | part |  | Opacity as a percentage. It sits in the picker's value row; add it to the row too if opacity should show without opening the picker. |
| messages | { mixed, open, area, hue, opacity, formats, … } |  | Replace the picker's text, for example to translate it. |

## Supported states

- mixed

- invalid

- read-only

- disabled

## Customization

Keep the committed fill in the host. Use change callbacks for live previews and the commit callback for updates to the document. Supply document swatches and your preferred picker parts. Eyedropper availability depends on the browser and a secure context. Keep direct color entry available.

~~~tsx
<ColorPicker label="Fill" value={fill} onValueCommit={setFill} className="font-mono" motion={false}>
  <ColorPickerField className="rounded-none"><ColorPickerLabel /><ColorPickerHexInput /><ColorPickerTrigger /></ColorPickerField>
  <ColorPickerContent className="rounded-none"><ColorPickerFields /><ColorPickerSwatches /></ColorPickerContent>
</ColorPicker>
~~~

Preserve keyboard access to the trigger and direct input. Verify alpha and format switching when wiring a custom parser or document color model.

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The swatch is a button named with the colour's label and value; the picker opens as a popover, or a bottom sheet on phones.

- The area and the hue and opacity sliders are sliders with readable values; arrow keys step them, Shift steps by 10, Home and End go to the ends.

- Every value can be typed: hex, red, green, blue, hue, saturation, lightness and opacity. A rejected value stays with a message.

- The eyedropper only appears where the browser supports it; it is never the only way to choose a colour.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/color-picker/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates.

If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry.

files.content: # Daily Task List Add, rename, reorder, complete and reopen tasks, and undo a delete. Built from Inline Edit, Context Menu and Sortable List; your app owns the tasks and every save. ## Release Version: 0.1.4. Status: experimental. License: MIT. ## Prerequisites Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package. React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported. ## Install Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version: ~~~sh npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/daily-task-list/0.1.4.json ~~~ For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs. ## Files and dependencies - @ui/daily-task-list-actions.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list-capture.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list-feedback.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list-root.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list-sections.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list-state.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list-title.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list.tsx - @ui/daily-task-list.md Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0, motion@14.6.0. Pinned registry dependencies: inline-edit@0.1.3, context-menu@0.1.2, sortable-list@0.1.3. ## Installed guide This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as daily-task-list.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates. ## Minimal working example This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence. ~~~tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { DailyTaskList, DailyTaskListHeader, DailyTaskListCapture, DailyTaskListActive, DailyTaskListCompleted, DailyTaskListEmpty, DailyTaskListFeedback, type DailyTask } from "@/components/ui/daily-task-list"; export default function DailyTaskListExample() { const [tasks, setTasks] = useState([ { id: "a", title: "Sketch the inspector", done: false }, { id: "b", title: "Review interactions", done: true }, ]); return ( { setTasks(current => [{ id: crypto.randomUUID(), title, done: false }, ...current]); }} onRename={async (task, title) => { setTasks(current => current.map(item => item.id === task.id ? { ...item, title } : item)); }} onToggle={async (task, done) => { setTasks(current => [...current.filter(item => item.id !== task.id), { ...task, done }]); }} onReorder={async (ordered, _move, section) => { setTasks(current => section === "active" ? [...ordered, ...current.filter(item => item.done)] : [...current.filter(item => !item.done), ...ordered]); }} onDelete={async task => { setTasks(current => current.filter(item => item.id !== task.id)); }} onRestore={async task => { setTasks(current => [task, ...current]); }}> ); } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | tasks | T extends { id, title, done }[] | | All of the day's tasks in your order; put new tasks first to show them at the top. Active and completed tasks show in separate sections. | | onToggle | (task: T, done: boolean) => void \| Promise | | Completing first strikes the title, then calls this; the task slides into Completed once you update tasks, landing where it sits in your order (move it to the end to show it at the bottom). A rejection retracts the strike. | | onCreate / onRename | (…) => void \| Promise | | Save a new task or a new title. A returned promise shows saving; rejecting keeps your data and offers Retry. | | onReorder | (ordered: T[], move, section) => void \| Promise | | Called once per completed move with the new order of that section ("active" or "completed"); each section keeps its own order. | | onDelete / onRestore | (task: T) => void \| Promise | | Delete a task, then restore it when the person presses Undo. | | validateTitle | (title: string) => string \| null | | Return a message to reject a title. Defaults to requiring a non-empty title. | | disabled | boolean | false | Shows the day without allowing changes. | | motion | boolean | true | Animation in every part. Turning it off never removes an action. Reduced motion is always honored. | | messages | Partial | | Replace labels and announcements, for example to translate them. | | portalContainer | HTMLElement \| null | | Where task menus render. Defaults to document.body. | | Header, Capture, Active, Completed, Empty, Feedback | parts | | Compose the ones you need. Header takes the day label; Active and Completed take renderMeta, renderActions and classNames for rows, checkboxes and menus. | | useDailyTaskList() | hook | | Active and completed tasks, busy IDs, the latest failure or deletion, and actions, for building your own parts. | ## Supported states - empty - all done - saving - error - disabled ## Composition and customization Install this Block to receive its three pinned UICoolKit Component dependencies automatically. The Block imports them by the same installed shadcn paths used in the consumer app. It adds no required UICoolKit runtime. Compose Header, Capture, Active, Empty, Completed and Feedback as needed. Active and Completed accept renderMeta, renderActions and part classNames; keep labels and actions accessible when replacing them. Rename uses Inline Edit's Ghost presentation. ~~~tsx {task.project}} /> Make room for one useful task. ~~~ Use the imports from the minimal example. This fragment assumes a task type extending DailyTask with project metadata and real host callbacks. ## Task model and callbacks The host owns IDs, titles, completion state and order. Use stable IDs. Return promises from create, rename, complete/reopen, reorder, delete and restore callbacks so pending and failures are represented correctly. Commit host state after persistence succeeds; a rejected action keeps the authoritative data and exposes recovery. Active and completed sections reorder separately. onReorder receives the section name and that section's new order; merge it back with the other section. Put newly created tasks first if desired. Append a newly completed task to the host list if it should appear last in Completed. Deletion exposes Undo through the host's restore action. Complete/reopen first animates the title, then hands the operation to the host; failed persistence retracts the visual change. There is no fake server success. Replace messages to translate labels/announcements, validateTitle to validate capture/rename and portalContainer to scope action menus to the host's theme. useDailyTaskList exposes state/actions for custom parts inside the root. disabled prevents edits across the composition. ## Motion and boundaries Set motion={false} to disable optional effects in the composed pieces; reduced motion is honored. Phone action menus use bottom sheets. Verify persistence rejection, retry, undo and multiple configured instances after connecting the host callbacks. A single host-labelled day only. {formatCubicBezier(curve)}
); } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | value | [x1, y1, x2, y2] | | The committed curve. Your app owns it. | | onValueCommit | (value, detail) => void | | Called once per finished drag, key press, field edit or preset. detail names the handle and source. | | onValueChange | (value, detail) => void | | Live curves, and the starting curve when a drag is cancelled. | | label | string | | The name shown above the curve and read by screen readers. | | range | [min, max] | [-0.25, 1.25] | The progress handles can reach. X always stays from 0 to 1. | | step | number | 0.01 | How far handles move. Shift moves ten steps. | | presets | { value, label, curve }[] | | Replaces the preset list. Linear, Ease, Ease in, Ease out and Ease in-out by default. | | duration / onDurationChange / onDurationCommit | number / functions | | Passing duration shows the Duration slider. Your app owns the value. | | durationRange | { min, max, step, unit } | 0 to 2, 0.01, s | The Duration slider's limits, step and unit. | | container | HTMLElement | | Where the preset menu is portalled. | | mixed | boolean | false | The selection holds different curves. Fields show Mixed, value is where editing starts, and the first edit commits. | | disabled / readOnly / motion / messages | boolean / boolean / boolean / object | | Turn off or lock editing; turn off the handles' press transition; replace the text. | | EasingCurveLabel / EasingCurvePresets / EasingCurveSurface / EasingCurveFields | parts | | Compose only what you need, such as the surface without fields. | | EasingCurveGrid / EasingCurveLine / EasingCurveHandlePoint | parts | | The grid, curve and a handle, placed inside the surface. | | EasingCurveEaseField / EasingCurveDurationField | parts | | All four numbers in one field, which also accepts cubic-bezier() and CSS keywords, and the Duration slider. | | EasingCurveGraph | part | | A read-only graph of any easing function, such as a spring your app calculates. | | formatCubicBezier / parseCubicBezier / cubicBezierAt | functions | | Convert to and from CSS, and read the progress at a moment. | | useEasingCurveEditor | hook | | The live curve and state, for custom parts. | ## Supported states - disabled ## Integration Store the cubic Bézier as a tuple and use formatCubicBezier for CSS. Compose the surface, presets and numeric fields where they fit the host. EasingCurveGraph also supports read-only rendering. Use onValueChange for a live preview and onValueCommit for undo or persistence. Run any animation separately in the host and honor its reduced-motion settings. ## Customization Style the graph independently of the fields with their className props. Supply your own preset list to match the motion tokens used in your application. ```tsx ``` ## Accessibility and integration checks - Each handle is a slider with its own tab stop. # Image Picker

An image row whose picker takes a chosen, dropped or pasted file, a link or a library image. Your app stores it; the picker shows progress, Cancel and Retry.

## Release

Version: 0.2.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/image-picker/0.2.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/image-picker-parts.tsx

- @ui/image-picker-root.tsx

- @ui/image-picker-state.tsx

- @ui/image-picker.tsx

- @ui/image-picker.md

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: none.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as image-picker.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  ImagePicker, ImagePickerContent, ImagePickerError, ImagePickerField, ImagePickerLabel, ImagePickerLibrary,
  ImagePickerName, ImagePickerThumbnail, ImagePickerUrlInput, type ImageValue,
} from "@/components/ui/image-picker";

export default function ImagePickerExample() {
  const [image, setImage] = useState<ImageValue | null>(null);
  return (
    <ImagePicker label="Fill image" value={image} onValueCommit={setImage}>
      <ImagePickerField><ImagePickerLabel /><ImagePickerName /><ImagePickerThumbnail /></ImagePickerField>
      <ImagePickerContent>
        <ImagePickerLibrary><ImagePickerUrlInput /></ImagePickerLibrary>
        <ImagePickerError />
      </ImagePickerContent>
    </ImagePicker>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| value | { src, name?, width?, height? } \| null |  | The committed image, or null for none. Your app owns it. |
| mixed | boolean |  | The selection holds different images; the row shows Mixed. |
| onValueCommit | (value) => void |  | Called once per finished change: an upload, a link, a library image, or null when removed. |
| onUpload | (file, { signal, onProgress }) => Promise<image> |  | Stores the file and resolves with where it lives. Report progress from 0 to 1, and stop when the signal aborts. Without it, the picker commits a local object URL that lasts only for the session. |
| library | { src, name? }[] |  | Images your app already has, such as recent uploads or assets, shown as a grid. |
| accept / maxSize | string[] / number | PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG | Allowed MIME types and the largest file in bytes. A file outside them shows a message and is not uploaded. |
| defaultOpen | boolean |  | Opens the picker on first render, such as right after a fill becomes an image. |
| disabled / readOnly / motion / container | boolean / HTMLElement |  | Turn off editing or opening; turn off transitions; portal the picker elsewhere. |
| ImagePickerField / Label / Name / Thumbnail | parts |  | The row: one button that opens the picker, with the label, the image's name (or Mixed, or Add image) and a small preview. |
| ImagePickerContent side / align / anchor | "bottom" \| "top" \| "left" \| "right" | "bottom" | Where the picker opens against the row; it flips rather than cover the row. A bottom sheet on phones. |
| ImagePickerLibrary columns / removable / children | number / boolean | 4 / true | The picker's grid, which doubles as its preview: an Upload tile, the file being uploaded (progress and ×), the current image when it is not in the library, then the library, with the current image marked. Drop files on it; Remove sits beside its heading, and children (such as the link field) sit between the heading and the grid. |
| ImagePickerDropArea / Actions | parts |  | A large drop area with Replace and Remove, for an image outside a panel, such as a cover image in a form. |
| ImagePickerError / UrlInput | parts |  | The last problem, with Retry for a failed upload; a field for a link. |
| messages | { empty, drop, choose, url, replace, remove, uploading, … } |  | Replace the picker's text, for example to translate it. |

## Supported states

- empty

- mixed

- read-only

- disabled

## Customization

The host owns storage and the committed image. Supply `onUpload` for file, drop and paste support. Honor its abort signal, report progress as a fraction, and return the stored image URL. Use the library prop for host-managed assets. Validate links in the host before saving them to your application. Keep the error part in the popup or drop area so a failed upload can be retried.

~~~tsx
<ImagePicker label="Cover" value={image} onValueCommit={setImage} onUpload={upload} motion={false} className="font-mono">
  <ImagePickerField className="rounded-none"><ImagePickerLabel /><ImagePickerName /><ImagePickerThumbnail /></ImagePickerField>
  <ImagePickerContent><ImagePickerLibrary><ImagePickerUrlInput /></ImagePickerLibrary><ImagePickerError /></ImagePickerContent>
</ImagePicker>
~~~

Verify link selection, cancellation, failed uploads and retry. On phones, confirm the picker fits the viewport and focus returns to its trigger when dismissed.

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The row is one button named after the image's label; the picker opens as a popover, or a bottom sheet on phones.

- Every source works from the keyboard: the Upload tile (or the empty drop area) opens the file dialog, and pasting an image or a link works while the row or picker has focus, which it takes when it opens.

- Upload progress is a progress bar with its value; errors are announced as alerts and describe the row and the link field.

- Library images are buttons named after each image, with the current one marked as pressed; an upload in progress has a named progress bar and a Cancel button.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

files.content: # Inline Edit Click a value to edit it where it sits. Enter saves, Escape cancels, and clicking away never saves by accident. The Ghost variant edits on top of the text with no buttons. ## Release Version: 0.1.3. Status: experimental. License: MIT. ## Prerequisites Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package. React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported. ## Install Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version: ~~~sh npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/inline-edit/0.1.3.json ~~~ For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs. ## Files and dependencies - @ui/inline-edit-feedback.tsx - @ui/inline-edit-field.tsx - @ui/inline-edit-root.tsx - @ui/inline-edit-state.tsx - @ui/inline-edit.tsx - @ui/inline-edit.md Npm dependencies: none beyond the host React/shadcn setup. Pinned registry dependencies: none. ## Installed guide This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as inline-edit.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates. ## Minimal working example This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence. ~~~tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { InlineEdit, InlineEditPreview, InlineEditEditor, InlineEditInput, InlineEditSave, InlineEditCancel, InlineEditError, InlineEditConflict } from "@/components/ui/inline-edit"; export default function InlineEditExample() { const [name, setName] = useState("Launch notes"); return ( { setName(next); }} validate={next => next.trim() ? null : "Enter a name."}> ); } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | value | string | | The committed value. Your app owns it and updates it after a successful save. | | onSave | (draft: string) => void \| Promise | | Persist the draft. A returned promise shows pending; rejecting keeps the draft and offers retry. | | label | string | | Accessible name of the field, such as “Task name”. | | validate | (draft: string) => string \| null \| undefined | | Return a message to reject the draft before saving. | | editing / defaultEditing | boolean | | Control edit mode yourself, or set where it starts. | | onEditingChange | (editing: boolean) => void | | Called when the user starts or finishes editing. | | onCancel | () => void | | Called after the user cancels an edit. | | disabled | boolean | false | Shows the value without allowing edits. | | motion | boolean | true | Entrance transitions for the editor and messages. Reduced motion is always honored. | | variant | "default" \| "ghost" | "default" | Ghost edits on top of the text itself: a line draws in under it, there are no Save or Cancel buttons, Enter saves and Escape cancels. | | saveOnBlur | boolean | true for ghost | Leaving the field saves a valid change; an unchanged or invalid one reverts. Off by default for the default variant, where leaving never saves. | | className | string | | Every part accepts className, merged after defaults so yours win. Parts expose data-editing, data-status, data-invalid and data-conflict. | | useInlineEdit() | hook | | State and actions of the nearest InlineEdit, for building your own parts. | ## Supported states - editing - invalid - pending - error - conflict - disabled ## Styling and replaced content Each part accepts native attributes, a forwarded ref and className merged after defaults. Keep the root's label meaningful. Replace the preview, action labels, error content or conflict content through children and render functions. ~~~tsx {value => {value || "Untitled workspace"}} {status => status === "pending" ? "Updating…" : "Update"} Keep original ~~~ Use the complete imports and application state pattern from the minimal example. This styling example changes both the appearance and content without patching internals. ## State and persistence The value prop is committed application state. Return the save promise and update value only after successful persistence; reject to retain the draft and show retry. Validate synchronously with validate. A changed external value during a dirty edit creates a conflict; include InlineEditConflict so the user can choose the latest value or keep the draft. Default mode uses explicit Save/Cancel and does not save when focus leaves. Ghost mode uses variant="ghost", omits action buttons when you choose, saves valid changes on blur by default and still supports Enter/Escape. Set saveOnBlur explicitly to change that policy. Use editing/onEditingChange for externally controlled edit mode, defaultEditing for an initial uncontrolled session, and useInlineEdit inside the root to build custom parts. Consumer handlers run before internal behavior where documented; preventDefault cancels the corresponding internal action. ## Motion and boundaries Set motion={false} to disable optional transitions. Reduced motion is honored independently. Single-line text only; no rich text, multiline editor or collaboration backend is provided. Pending saves remain focusable and cannot be submitted twice. ## Accessibility and integration checks - The value is a native button; activating it focuses the input and selects its text. - Enter saves unless an input method is composing; Escape cancels. Leaving the field never saves in the default variant; in ghost it saves a valid change and reverts an invalid one. - Validation and save errors use role=alert and are linked to the input with aria-describedby. - Save stays focusable while pending (aria-disabled, aria-busy), and focus returns to the value after save or cancel. - Entrance transitions are skipped with reduced motion or motion={false}. Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling. ## Updates and conflicts Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/inline-edit/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. # Layers Panel

A design tool's layer tree with frames nested to any depth. Search by name, select like a canvas, rename in place, drag layers between frames, and hide or lock them.

## Release

Version: 0.2.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Migration

Remove messages.count from message overrides. Replace useLayersPanel().total with a count derived from the app-owned layer tree. To keep a count in the header, render it as a LayersPanelHeader child.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/layers-panel/0.2.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/layers-panel-children.tsx

- @ui/layers-panel-root.tsx

- @ui/layers-panel-row.tsx

- @ui/layers-panel-state.tsx

- @ui/layers-panel-tree.tsx

- @ui/layers-panel.tsx

- @ui/layers-panel.md

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: context-menu@0.1.2, inline-edit@0.1.3.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as layers-panel.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  LayersPanel, LayersPanelEmpty, LayersPanelHeader, LayersPanelIcon, LayersPanelName, LayersPanelSearch,
  LayersPanelTree, moveLayer, type LayersPanelLayer,
} from "@/components/ui/layers-panel";

const initial: LayersPanelLayer[] = [
  { id: "home", name: "Home", children: [{ id: "title", name: "Title" }] },
  { id: "settings", name: "Settings" },
];

export default function LayersPanelExample() {
  const [layers, setLayers] = useState(initial);
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([]);
  return (
    <LayersPanel
      className="h-64"
      layers={layers}
      selected={selected}
      onSelectedChange={setSelected}
      onMove={move => setLayers(current => moveLayer(current, move))}
    >
      <LayersPanelHeader />
      <LayersPanelSearch />
      <LayersPanelTree>
        {layer => <><LayersPanelIcon kind={layer.children ? "frame" : "text"} /><LayersPanelName /></>}
      </LayersPanelTree>
      <LayersPanelEmpty />
    </LayersPanel>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| layers | { id, name, children?, hidden?, locked? }[] |  | The top-level layers, each holding its own children to any depth. The panel never changes them itself. |
| selected / onSelectedChange | string[] / (ids) => void |  | The selected ids, and the selection a click asks for: one layer, Cmd/Ctrl to add or remove, Shift for a range of visible layers. |
| onRename / validate | (layer, name) => void \| Promise |  | Saves a new name; a rejected promise keeps editing with an error. Omit onRename to turn renaming off. |
| onMove | ({ layer, from, to }) => void |  | Saves a finished move, within a frame or into another, once per drop or key press. moveLayer(layers, move) applies it to your tree. Moving pauses while searching. |
| onHiddenChange / onLockedChange | (layer, value) => void |  | Show and save the hide and lock toggles. Active toggles stay visible; others appear on hover or focus. |
| actions | (layer) => ReactNode |  | Extra right-click menu items for a layer, after Rename, the moves and the toggles. |
| defaultCollapsed | string[] |  | Ids of layers whose children start collapsed. |
| childrenStatus | "unloaded" \| "loading" \| "failed" |  | Set on a layer whose children your app loads on demand. It shows a chevron before they exist; clear it once they load. |
| onExpandedChange / onRetryChildren | (layer, expanded) => void / (layer) => void |  | Report each open or close, for loading children, and add Retry to a group that failed to load. |
| LayersPanelTree / Icon / Name / Toggles / Status | parts |  | The scrolling tree and its row parts. Icon shows the layer's kind and becomes the drag handle on hover. rowClassName styles every row through its data-selected, data-hidden, data-locked and data-drop attributes. |
| disabled / motion / container | boolean / HTMLElement |  | Turn off every interaction; turn off transitions (reduced motion is always honored); portal menus and tooltips elsewhere. |
| messages | { label, search, empty, noResults, … } |  | Replace the panel's text, for example to translate it. |

## Supported states

- empty

- error

- disabled

## Customization

Use stable IDs for every layer, including descendants. Keep selection and the layer tree in app state. Apply move requests with `moveLayer` or the host's equivalent tree operation. Persist rename, visibility and lock in their respective callbacks. Render app-specific row content alongside the supplied name, icon and toggle parts.

~~~tsx
<LayersPanel layers={layers} selected={selected} onSelectedChange={select} className="h-72 rounded-none font-mono" motion={false}>
  <LayersPanelSearch />
  <LayersPanelTree>{() => <LayersPanelName />}</LayersPanelTree>
  <LayersPanelEmpty />
</LayersPanel>
~~~

For large or remote trees, set `childrenStatus: "unloaded"` on a group and load its children from `onExpandedChange`. Set it to `"loading"` or `"failed"` while that runs, pass `onRetryChildren` to offer Retry, and clear it once `children` is ready. An empty frame without a status has no chevron.

Preserve focus and test a keyboard move between frames, filtering, and the locked-layer restriction alongside pointer dragging.

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The panel is a region named “Layers”; the search field is a labelled search box, and Escape clears it.

- Each name is a toggle button that reports whether the layer is selected; F2 or a double click renames it.

- Frames have disclosure buttons named “Expand” or “Collapse”; collapsed layers are inert, so Tab skips them.

- Groups that load on demand announce loading and failure, and Retry names the group.

- Hide and lock are toggle buttons with the layer's name; they are also in the right-click menu.

- Moving never needs a drag: on the handle, Up and Down move among siblings, Left moves out of the frame and Right into the frame above; the menu offers the same moves. Each move is announced.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/layers-panel/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates.

If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry.

## License

MIT. Dependencies retain their respective licenses.

# Motion Inspector

Edit how a selected item animates with an easing curve or a spring set by time or physics. Each edit commits once, and Replay lets your app play the result.

## Release

Version: 0.1.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

~~~sh

~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/motion-inspector-editors.tsx

- @ui/motion-inspector-math.ts

- @ui/motion-inspector-parts.tsx

- @ui/motion-inspector-root.tsx

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as motion-inspector.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { MotionInspector, type MotionValue } from "@/components/ui/motion-inspector";

export default function MotionInspectorExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<MotionValue>({ type: "spring", definedBy: "time", duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2 });
  return <MotionInspector className="max-w-sm rounded-xl border border-border p-4" label="Entrance transition" value={value} onValueCommit={setValue} />;
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| value | MotionValue \| null |  | The committed easing or spring, or null when nothing is selected. Your app owns it. Include delay to show the Delay field. |
| onValueCommit | (value, detail) => void |  | Called once per finished edit. detail names the field that changed. |
| onValueChange | (value, detail) => void |  | Live values while dragging, and the committed value when a drag is cancelled. |
| onReplay | () => void |  | Shows Replay. Your app plays the transition; the panel runs no animation. |
| label | string |  | The panel's visible and accessible name. |
| mixed | boolean | false | Selected items differ. Fields show Mixed, value is where editing starts, and the first edit commits a complete value for all of them. |
| ranges | Partial<MotionRanges> |  | Limits, steps and units for Duration, Delay, Bounce, Stiffness, Damping and Mass. |
| container | HTMLElement |  | Where the preset menu and tooltip are portalled. |
| disabled / readOnly / messages | boolean / boolean / object |  | Turn off or lock editing; replace the text. |
| MotionInspectorHeader / Mode / Easing / Spring / Delay / Empty / Replay | parts |  | Compose only what you need, or reorder the panel. |
| MotionInspectorSpringGraph | part |  | A read-only curve of a spring. |
| springAt / springSettleTime / motionDuration | functions |  | Read a spring's progress and length, for your own playback. |
| springToPhysics / springToTime | functions |  | Convert a spring between its two forms. |
| useMotionInspector | hook |  | The value and state, for custom parts. |

## Supported states

- empty

- mixed

- disabled

## Integration

Represent a transition as MotionValue and pass null when nothing is selected. Set mixed for multiple selected transitions with different values and use commit detail to apply only the edited property.

Wire onReplay to the host animation. Use onValueChange for a live preview and onValueCommit for a single saved edit. Respect reduced motion in the host preview.

## Customization

Dock the editor in an inspector or place it next to a preview. Use the className prop for width and surface, and messages to give host-specific names to motion modes.

```tsx
<MotionInspector label="Entrance" value={transition} onValueCommit={save} className="max-w-xs rounded-2xl bg-muted p-3" />
```

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The Animation and Type switches are radio groups operated with the arrow keys.

- Every value is a slider that also accepts typing, and each key press commits once.

- Escape cancels a drag and restores the committed value.

- The spring curve has a text name, and its values stay available in the fields beside it.

- Replay is a named button, and your app decides how to honor reduced motion when it plays.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

# Notification Stack

Keep the newest notification in front. Fan out the deck to read each message, dismiss one at a time, or open the full list.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { NotificationStack, type StackNotification } from "@/components/ui/notification-stack";

export default function NotificationStackExample() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<StackNotification[]>([]);
  return <>
    <NotificationStack items={items} onDismiss={id => setItems(previous => previous.filter(item => item.id !== id))} />
    <button type="button" onClick={() => setItems(previous => [...previous, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), title: "Changes saved" }])}>Notify</button>
  </>;
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| items / onDismiss | StackNotification[] / (id: string) => void |  | Supply active messages oldest first with stable unique IDs. Remove a message when the stack requests dismissal by button or timeout. |
| title / description / icon / tone | Item fields |  | Give each message a title, optional details and icon. Set tone to error for urgent announcements. |
| duration | number | 5000 | Milliseconds before dismissal. Override per item, or use 0 to keep it until dismissed. Each timer resumes with its remaining time. |
| visible / position | number / "top" \| "bottom" |  | The compact deck shows the newest three messages by default. Position chooses which edge holds the newest card. The host places the stack. |
| defaultExpanded / motion | boolean |  | Start with the full list open, or turn off the deck's layout animation. |
| className / cardClassName / emptyIcon | string / string / ReactNode |  | The deck reserves 20rem and expands upward from its base. Lists taller than 75% of the viewport scroll. Override the reserved height, style cards, or supply the empty state's icon. |

## Supported states

- stacked

- expanded

- empty

## Integration

Keep notification data in host state and append new items with stable IDs. Remove the requested ID in the dismissal callback. Give persistent messages a duration of zero.

## Customization

The deck reserves 20rem and expands upward from its base. Lists taller than 75% of the viewport scroll. Override the reserved height, style cards, or supply the empty state's icon.

```tsx
<NotificationStack items={items} onDismiss={dismiss}
  duration={0} visible={4} position="top" motion={false}
  className="max-w-md" cardClassName="rounded-md bg-secondary"
/>
```

- Show all works with keyboard, mouse and touch. Each dismiss button names its notification.

- Cards wrap long text and follow system reduced-motion settings.

"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { NotificationStack, type StackNotification } from "@/components/ui/notification-stack";

export default function NotificationStackExample() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<StackNotification[]>([]);

    <NotificationStack items={items} onDismiss={id => setItems(previous => previous.filter(item => item.id !== id))} />

~~~

|---|---|---|---|

# Number Field

Edit a number the way design tools do: type it, step it, or drag its label or number, as an input or a slider. Drags preview live and commit once when you let go.

## Release

Version: 0.2.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/number-field/0.2.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/number-field-input.tsx

- @ui/number-field-keyword.tsx

- @ui/number-field-root.tsx

- @ui/number-field-scrub.tsx

- @ui/number-field-slider-parts.tsx

- @ui/number-field-slider.tsx

- @ui/number-field-state.tsx

- @ui/number-field-stepper.tsx

- @ui/number-field-value.tsx

- @ui/number-field.tsx

- @ui/number-field.md

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: none.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as number-field.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  NumberField, NumberFieldDecrement, NumberFieldError, NumberFieldGroup, NumberFieldIncrement,
  NumberFieldInput, NumberFieldLabel, NumberFieldScrubArea, NumberFieldStepper, NumberFieldUnit,
} from "@/components/ui/number-field";

export default function NumberFieldExample() {
  const [width, setWidth] = useState<number | null>(320);
  return (
    <NumberField label="Width" value={width} onValueCommit={setWidth} min={0} max={1440} unit="px">
      <NumberFieldScrubArea><NumberFieldLabel /></NumberFieldScrubArea>
      <NumberFieldGroup>
        <NumberFieldInput />
        <NumberFieldUnit />
        <NumberFieldStepper><NumberFieldIncrement /><NumberFieldDecrement /></NumberFieldStepper>
      </NumberFieldGroup>
      <NumberFieldError />
    </NumberField>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| value | number \| keyword \| null |  | The committed value: a number, or one of your keywords. Your app owns it; null means there is none, such as a mixed selection. |
| onValueCommit | (value: number \| keyword) => void |  | Called once per finished change: a typed value, a step, the end of a drag, or a keyword. |
| onValueChange | (value: number) => void |  | Called with every change, including live values while dragging. A cancelled drag sends the committed value back. |
| label | string |  | Accessible name of the field, such as “Width”. |
| min / max | number |  | Limits. A typed value outside them is rejected with a message naming the limit; stepping and dragging stop at them. The slider needs both. |
| step / largeStep | number | 1 / step × 10 | Arrow keys and buttons move by step; Shift and Page Up/Down by largeStep. |
| precision | number | decimals of step | Decimal places kept and shown. |
| unit | string |  | Shown after the value and read with it, such as “px”. Typing the unit is accepted. |
| format / parse | (value: number) => string / (text: string) => number |  | Replace how values are shown and read. Return NaN from parse to reject text. |
| validate | (value: number) => string \| null \| undefined |  | Return a message to reject a typed value; the text stays for fixing. |
| keywords | { value, label, resolved? }[] |  | Named values the field can also hold, such as Auto, Hug or Fill. One with a resolved number shows it beside its name; typing a keyword's name selects it. |
| keywordFallback | number | min, or 0 | Where stepping or dragging starts from a keyword with no resolved number. Adjusting a keyword always turns it into a number. |
| NumberFieldKeywordMenu | { compact } |  | The menu at the end of the group: Fixed and your keywords. Opens as a bottom sheet on phones; container sets where it is portalled. compact shows only the arrow for Fixed, for narrow fields. |
| submitText / editText | (text) => true \| string \| void / string |  | Read your own typed forms before the field parses a number, such as a list of values: return true when applied or a message to reject. editText is what typing starts from when the value is empty. |
| placeholder | string |  | Shown when value is null, such as “Mixed”. Stepping and dragging need a value; typing sets one. |
| disabled / readOnly | boolean | false | Disabled cannot be focused; read-only shows the value and can be focused. |
| sensitivity | number | 4 | Pixels of drag per step on a scrub area. |
| stepperLayout | "auto" \| "stacked" \| "split" | "auto" | Where the stepper's buttons go: small up/down arrows at the end, or larger − and + on either side. Auto chooses split on touch screens, in CSS, so it never flashes. Parts expose data-layout for styling. |
| motion | boolean | true | The slider fill glides between stepped values. Reduced motion is always honored. |
| messages | { invalid, tooLow, tooHigh, increment, decrement, fixed, mode } |  | Replace the invalid-number and limit messages ({min} and {max} become the formatted limit with its unit), the step buttons' names and the keyword menu's text. |
| className | string |  | Every part accepts className, merged after defaults so yours win. Parts expose data-dragging, data-typing, data-invalid, data-empty, data-disabled and data-readonly. |
| NumberFieldSliderSteps markClassName | string |  | Styles each step mark; marks under the fill have data-filled. Marks show while adjusting and use large steps when there would be more than 40. |
| useNumberField() | hook |  | State and actions of the nearest NumberField, for building your own parts. |

## Supported states

- mixed

- invalid

- disabled

- read-only

## Customization

Keep the committed number in application state. Use `onValueChange` for drag or slider previews and `onValueCommit` for updates to the stored value. Clear any temporary preview after cancellation. Use a keyword configuration for values such as Auto or Fill and keep the chosen keyword in the host model.

~~~tsx
<NumberField label="Width" defaultValue={320} className="rounded-none font-mono" motion={false}>
  <NumberFieldGroup className="border-dashed"><NumberFieldInput /></NumberFieldGroup>
  <NumberFieldError />
</NumberField>
~~~

Keep the error part near the input, and give a standalone scrub area or slider an accessible label.

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The input is a spin button and the slider presentation a slider, both named by label, with the unit in their value text.

- Enter commits a typed value unless an input method is composing; Escape reverts it. Invalid text stays with a role=alert message linked by aria-describedby.

- Arrow keys step, Shift and Page Up/Down take large steps; on the slider, Home and End go to the limits and Enter or F2 opens typing.

- Dragging is never the only way to change a value. Escape cancels a drag; on touch, vertical movement scrolls the page.

- The stepper arrows stay out of the tab order because the arrow keys do the same thing, and pressing them keeps focus in the input. Holding one repeats, previewing live and committing once on release.

- Fill transitions are skipped with reduced motion or motion={false}.

- A keyword is read with the value, such as 240 px, Hug. The keyword menu is a labelled select (Width mode), and a keyword can also be typed.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Place a logo at the center of a field of orbiting dots or icons. Hover to pulse the accent dots or light a ring around each icon.

## Release

|---|---|---|---|
| rings | number \| readonly OrbitRing[] | 3 | Choose one to six rings or supply their radii and dot counts. Radii use a 260-unit square. Offset sets the starting angle in degrees. |
| center | ReactNode |  | Replace the center dot with a logo, avatar or icon. |
| renderNode | (node: OrbitNode) => ReactNode |  | Use the zero-based ring and dot index and the ring’s dot count to replace selected dots. Icons stay upright. Return null to keep a dot. |
| synchronized | boolean | false | Rotate rings together at the same speed to preserve angular spacing between icons. |
| still / speed | boolean / number | false / 1 | Freeze and resume the current pose, or change the rotation rate. |
| interactive | boolean | true | Pulse accent dots on pointer entry, or show a dim white glow that follows each orbiting icon’s silhouette while hovered. |

| label | string |  | Give an informative illustration a single accessible name. |

<OrbitField center={<ProductMark />} label="Product and connected apps"
