items.description: Play, rewind, seek and set the volume of anything your app plays.

files.content:
# Playback Controls

Music-player style controls for animation, video or audio your app runs: play, rewind, seek, loop, speed and volume. Compose only the parts you need.

## Release

Version: 0.1.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/playback-controls/0.1.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/playback-controls-buttons.tsx

- @ui/playback-controls-root.tsx

- @ui/playback-controls-scrub.ts

- @ui/playback-controls-seek.tsx

- @ui/playback-controls-settings.tsx

- @ui/playback-controls-state.tsx

- @ui/playback-controls-time.ts

- @ui/playback-controls-volume.tsx

- @ui/playback-controls.tsx

- @ui/playback-controls.md

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: inspector-field@0.2.0.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as playback-controls.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { PlaybackControls } from "@/components/ui/playback-controls";

export default function PlaybackControlsExample() {
  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);
  const [time, setTime] = useState(0);
  return (
    <PlaybackControls className="rounded-xl border border-border p-3" label="Preview playback"
      playing={playing} onPlayingChange={setPlaying} duration={10} currentTime={time}
      onSeek={setTime} onSeekCommit={setTime} />
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| label | string |  | Names the controls for screen readers. |
| playing / onPlayingChange | boolean / function |  | Whether playback runs. Your app owns it and starts or stops playback. |
| currentTime | number |  | The position in seconds. Your app owns it. |
| duration | number \| null |  | The length in seconds. Seeking is off while it is null. |
| onSeekCommit | (time, detail) => void |  | Called once per finished drag, key press or button. detail names the source. |
| onSeek | (time, detail) => void |  | Live positions, and the starting position when a drag is cancelled. |
| onScrubbingChange | (scrubbing) => void |  | Called when a drag starts and ends, so your app can hold playback. |
| step / largeStep | number | 0.1 / 1 | Seconds moved by arrow keys and small step buttons, and by Rewind, Fast forward, Shift or Page keys. |
| volume / onVolumeChange / onVolumeCommit | number / functions |  | A level from 0 to 1. Passing volume shows a button that opens a vertical slider. Your app owns it. |
| muted / onMutedChange | boolean / function |  | For an app with its own mute: shows the level as 0, and raising it asks your app to unmute. |
| loop / onLoopChange | boolean / function |  | Passing loop shows the Loop button. With it on, Play never becomes Replay. |
| speed / onSpeedChange / speeds | number / function / number[] | 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 | Passing speed shows the Speed menu. |
| formatTime | (seconds) => string |  | Replaces the 0:01.20 time format. |
| loading / disabled | boolean |  | Wait for media with a spinner, or turn the controls off. |
| container / messages | HTMLElement / object |  | Where tooltips and the menu are portalled, and replacement text. |
| PlaybackPlayButton / PlaybackRestartButton / PlaybackStepButton / PlaybackLoopButton | parts |  | The buttons. PlaybackStepButton takes direction, and size: large for Rewind and Fast forward, small for fine steps. |
| PlaybackSeek / PlaybackTime / PlaybackSpeed / PlaybackVolume / PlaybackControlsRow | parts |  | The seek bar, time readout (show: both, current or duration), speed menu, volume popup and a row to lay parts out. |
| PlaybackTransport | part |  | The full button row. On phones and in narrow spaces: Restart, Rewind, Play, Fast forward and Settings, with Volume, Loop and Speed inside Settings. |
| PlaybackOptions / PlaybackSettings | parts |  | Options that fold into Settings when narrow, and the Settings menu itself. It opens as a bottom sheet on phones. |
| formatPlaybackTime / usePlaybackControls | function / hook |  | The default time format, and the state and actions for custom parts. |

## Supported states

- loading

- disabled

## Integration

Wire playing, currentTime and duration to media or a timeline owned by the host. Compose PlaybackControlsRow and the individual buttons when the full player layout is unnecessary.

Use onSeek for scrubbing and onSeekCommit to finalize playback position. Pass loop, speed and volume state only when the host supports them. The host advances time and applies playback settings.

## Customization

Use root className to dock the controls. Put secondary actions in PlaybackOptions so narrow layouts retain touch-sized transport controls.

```tsx
<PlaybackControlsRow className="w-full justify-center rounded-full border border-border p-2" />
```

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The controls form one labelled group, and every icon button has a name.

- Play's name changes to Pause, Replay or Loading with its state. Loop reports whether it is on.

- The seek bar is a slider that reads the position and length. Arrow keys step, Shift and Page keys take larger steps, and Home and End jump to the ends.

- The volume slider reads its level as a percentage and uses the same keys.

- Escape cancels a drag and returns to the starting position or level.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/playback-controls/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates.

If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry.

## License

MIT. Dependencies retain their respective licenses.

files.content:
# Property Inspector

Grouped properties for whatever is selected on your canvas. Shared values show as they are, differing ones as Mixed, and an edit applies to every selected item.

## Release

Version: 0.2.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/property-inspector/0.2.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/property-inspector-controls.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector-fields.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector-group.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector-list.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector-property.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector-root.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector-state.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector.tsx

- @ui/property-inspector.md

Npm dependencies: @base-ui/react@1.9.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: alignment-control@0.2.0, color-picker@0.2.0, image-picker@0.2.0, inspector-field@0.2.0, number-field@0.2.0, split-number-field@0.2.0.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as property-inspector.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import {
  applyPropertyChange, PropertyInspector, PropertyInspectorEmpty, PropertyInspectorGrid,
  PropertyInspectorGroup, PropertyInspectorHeader, PropertyInspectorNumber, PropertyInspectorText,
} from "@/components/ui/property-inspector";

export default function PropertyInspectorExample() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState([{ id: "home", name: "Home", width: 320 }]);
  return (
    <PropertyInspector items={items} onCommit={change => setItems(current => current.map(item => applyPropertyChange(item, change)))}>
      <PropertyInspectorHeader />
      <PropertyInspectorEmpty />
      <PropertyInspectorGroup title="Layout">
        <PropertyInspectorGrid>
          <PropertyInspectorText property="name" label="Name" single />
          <PropertyInspectorNumber property="width" label="Width" unit="px" min={1} />
        </PropertyInspectorGrid>
      </PropertyInspectorGroup>
    </PropertyInspector>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| items | { id: string }[] |  | The current selection. Your app owns it and the values; rows read each item's properties by key. |
| onCommit | ({ ids, property, value, changed?, insert?, remove? }) => void |  | Called once per finished edit with every selected id, so one edit is one undo step. property may be a path into a list, such as fills.0.color; changed names the parts set, insert and remove add or drop one list entry. |
| onPreview | ({ ids, property, value, changed? }) => void |  | Live values while a value is dragged or held, for moving or resizing on your canvas before the commit. |
| applyPropertyChange(item, change) | function |  | Returns the item with a change applied: at its path, part by part when it names parts, or as one added or removed list entry, so each item keeps the rest. |
| PropertyInspectorGroup | { title, defaultOpen, open, onOpenChange, actions } |  | A collapsible group; closed groups keep their fields out of the tab order. actions puts buttons in its header. A group inside a group is a sub-group. |
| Optional group | { present, onAdd, onRemove } |  | present says whether an item has the group, such as Flex. Its fields read and edit only those items; + and − report the ids that lack or have it. |
| PropertyInspectorGroupAction | { label, icon, onAction } |  | A small icon button for a group's header, such as + to add another fill, with a tooltip. |
| PropertyInspectorGrid | { columns } |  | The compact form: rows become cells of a grid (three columns by default) with their labels inside. A group can mix a grid and plain rows. |
| PropertyInspectorList | { property, label, create, visibleKey, shared, actions, children } |  | A list such as Fills, Borders or Shadows: + adds create() on top; entries have hide and remove. shared holds rows every entry shares, such as a border's width. Lists that differ in length show a note, and + replaces them. |
| PropertyInspectorSettings | { label, variant, summary, leading, children } |  | Settings in a popover, or a bottom sheet on phones: a row showing a summary such as Drop shadow, or with variant "icon" a header button, such as a border's position and style. Rows inside edit the same item or entry. |
| PropertyInspectorRow | part |  | Places related fields side by side in one line, such as X and Y or W and H; without it, fields stack. Each field keeps its own label and message. |
| Row options | { property, label, parts, single, locked, reason, hint, readOnly } |  | Every row takes these. parts reads a property part by part, so only differing parts show Mixed; single makes a property unavailable for several items, such as a name. |
| Grid options | { shortLabel, span, rowSpan } |  | In a grid: the short label or icon shown inside the field (the full label is still read, and an icon shows it in a tooltip on hover), and how many columns and rows the cell covers. |
| PropertyInspectorField | { children: (binding) => ReactNode, ownLabel } |  | The generic row: hosts any control with the property's value (null when Mixed), mixedParts, preview and commit, inside an Inspector Field. |
| PropertyInspectorText / Number / Value | row |  | A text, number (unit, min, max, step and keywords such as Auto or Hug) or read-only row. |
| PropertyInspectorSelect | { options, searchable, renderOption } |  | A choice from a list, such as Weight; searchable adds a search field for long lists such as Font family, with inspectorFieldFontOption showing each font in its face. |
| PropertyInspectorSegments / Toggle / ToggleButton / Checkbox | row |  | Built-in rows for a few choices, on/off segments, an icon button that stays pressed, and a checkbox with an optional shortcut. |
| Icon column | layout |  | Every group keeps two 32px icon slots at the right, so fields end on one line: visibility and remove, + and the chevron, and Split Number Field's expand button sit in them. Popovers have none. |
| PropertyInspectorSplitNumber / Alignment / Color | row |  | Built-in rows for a value made of parts (a Split Number Field preset), a 3×3 Alignment Grid and a colour that opens the Color Picker. |
| PropertyInspectorActions / Action | { label } / { label, icon, shortcut, onAction } |  | One-shot actions on the selection, such as Rotate 90° and the flips. Each press calls onAction once with every selected id; nothing stays pressed. |
| PropertyInspectorHeader / Empty | parts |  | The selection's title (the item's name or “2 selected”) and the empty state shown when nothing is selected. |
| labelPosition | "outside" \| "inside" |  | Where every row's label sits: its own column (the default), or inside one box per row, as many design tools do. |
| container | HTMLElement \| null |  | Where pickers and menus are portalled. Defaults to document.body. |
| density | "default" \| "compact" |  | Compact uses 28px filled fields and body-style group titles. The --uicoolkit-field-* CSS variables fine-tune either density. |
| disabled / motion | boolean |  | Disable every field; turn off group and field transitions. Reduced motion is always honored. |
| messages | { label, empty, mixed, multiple, single, add, remove, hide, show, mixedList } |  | Replace the panel's text: its name, the empty state, Mixed, the multiple-selection title, the single-item reason, + and −, a list entry's hide and show names, and the note for lists that differ. |
| usePropertyInspectorProperty() | hook |  | The binding the generic row uses, for building a row of your own around any control. |

## Supported states

- locked

- disabled

## Customization

Pass the host's current selection to `items` and choose which groups and controls to render. Use `onPreview` for ephemeral canvas feedback and `onCommit` to apply the final change once to the affected IDs. `applyPropertyChange` is available for immutable updates. Use the grid for mixed-width cells, list parts for repeatable entries, and custom field bindings for application-specific data. Image rows receive the host's upload callback and image library.

~~~tsx
<PropertyInspector items={selection} onCommit={commit} motion={false} className="max-w-sm rounded-none">
  <PropertyInspectorHeader />
  <PropertyInspectorEmpty />
  <PropertyInspectorGroup title="Spacing" className="border-t border-dashed">
    <PropertyInspectorNumber property="gap" label="Gap" unit="px" min={0} />
  </PropertyInspectorGroup>
</PropertyInspector>
~~~

Use `density="compact"` for dense panels. To match your own fields, set these CSS variables on the inspector or any ancestor: `--uicoolkit-field-height`, `--uicoolkit-field-bg`, `--uicoolkit-field-border`, `--uicoolkit-field-shadow`, `--uicoolkit-field-icon-bg`, `--uicoolkit-field-icon-border` and `--uicoolkit-field-icon-width`. Inner controls follow the field height. Inspector Field, Number Field, Alignment Control, Color Picker and Split Number Field read the same variables when used on their own.

Test an empty selection, matching values, mixed values and edits to a subset of the selection. Keep locked reasons available when supplying custom rows.

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The inspector is a region named “Properties”; the selection title updates politely when the selection changes.

- Groups are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded; collapsed content is inert, so hidden fields are skipped by Tab.

- Every row is an Inspector Field: labels name their controls, and Mixed, locked and unavailable states are announced with their reasons.

- A property made of parts shows Mixed only in the parts that differ, and each part is named with the property, such as “Padding top”.

- In the compact grid a field may show only “X” or an icon, but it is still named in full, such as “Rotation”; one-shot actions form a toolbar with one tab stop.

- An optional group's + and − are named, such as “Add Flex” and “Remove Flex”, with tooltips; a group with no items hides its fields from the tab order.

- Each list entry is a group named such as “Fill 2”, with named hide, show and remove buttons; a hidden entry stays editable. A settings row opens a dialog named after it, and Escape returns focus to the row.

- Numbers can be typed, stepped with the arrow keys or dragged; dragging is never the only way to change a value.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/property-inspector/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates.

If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry.

      <PropertyInspectorEmpty />
      <PropertyInspectorGroup title="Layout">
        <PropertyInspectorGrid>
          <PropertyInspectorText property="name" label="Name" single />
          <PropertyInspectorNumber property="width" label="Width" unit="px" min={1} />
        </PropertyInspectorGrid>
      </PropertyInspectorGroup>
    </PropertyInspector>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| items | { id: string }[] |  | The current selection. Your app owns it and the values; rows read each item's properties by key. |
| onCommit | ({ ids, property, value, changed?, insert?, remove? }) => void |  | Called once per finished edit with every selected id, so one edit is one undo step. property may be a path into a list, such as fills.0.color; changed names the parts set, insert and remove add or drop one list entry. |
| onPreview | ({ ids, property, value, changed? }) => void |  | Live values while a value is dragged or held, for moving or resizing on your canvas before the commit. |
| applyPropertyChange(item, change) | function |  | Returns the item with a change applied: at its path, part by part when it names parts, or as one added or removed list entry, so each item keeps the rest. |
| PropertyInspectorGroup | { title, defaultOpen, open, onOpenChange, actions } |  | A collapsible group; closed groups keep their fields out of the tab order. actions puts buttons in its header. A group inside a group is a sub-group. |
| Optional group | { present, onAdd, onRemove } |  | present says whether an item has the group, such as Flex. Its fields read and edit only those items; + and − report the ids that lack or have it. |
| PropertyInspectorGroupAction | { label, icon, onAction } |  | A small icon button for a group's header, such as + to add another fill, with a tooltip. |
| PropertyInspectorGrid | { columns } |  | The compact form: rows become cells of a grid (three columns by default) with their labels inside. A group can mix a grid and plain rows. |
| PropertyInspectorList | { property, label, create, visibleKey, shared, actions, children } |  | A list such as Fills, Borders or Shadows: + adds create() on top; entries have hide and remove. shared holds rows every entry shares, such as a border's width. Lists that differ in length show a note, and + replaces them. |
| PropertyInspectorSettings | { label, variant, summary, leading, children } |  | Settings in a popover, or a bottom sheet on phones: a row showing a summary such as Drop shadow, or with variant "icon" a header button, such as a border's position and style. Rows inside edit the same item or entry. |
| PropertyInspectorRow | part |  | Places related fields side by side in one line, such as X and Y or W and H; without it, fields stack. Each field keeps its own label and message. |
| Row options | { property, label, parts, single, locked, reason, hint, readOnly } |  | Every row takes these. parts reads a property part by part, so only differing parts show Mixed; single makes a property unavailable for several items, such as a name. |
| Grid options | { shortLabel, span, rowSpan } |  | In a grid: the short label or icon shown inside the field (the full label is still read, and an icon shows it in a tooltip on hover), and how many columns and rows the cell covers. |
| PropertyInspectorField | { children: (binding) => ReactNode, ownLabel } |  | The generic row: hosts any control with the property's value (null when Mixed), mixedParts, preview and commit, inside an Inspector Field. |
| PropertyInspectorText / Number / Value | row |  | A text, number (unit, min, max, step and keywords such as Auto or Hug) or read-only row. |
| PropertyInspectorSelect | { options, searchable, renderOption } |  | A choice from a list, such as Weight; searchable adds a search field for long lists such as Font family, with inspectorFieldFontOption showing each font in its face. |
| PropertyInspectorSegments / Toggle / ToggleButton / Checkbox | row |  | Built-in rows for a few choices, on/off segments, an icon button that stays pressed, and a checkbox with an optional shortcut. |
| Icon column | layout |  | Every group keeps two 32px icon slots at the right, so fields end on one line: visibility and remove, + and the chevron, and Split Number Field's expand button sit in them. Popovers have none. |
| PropertyInspectorSplitNumber / Alignment / Color | row |  | Built-in rows for a value made of parts (a Split Number Field preset), a 3×3 Alignment Grid and a colour that opens the Color Picker. |
| PropertyInspectorActions / Action | { label } / { label, icon, shortcut, onAction } |  | One-shot actions on the selection, such as Rotate 90° and the flips. Each press calls onAction once with every selected id; nothing stays pressed. |
| PropertyInspectorHeader / Empty | parts |  | The selection's title (the item's name or “2 selected”) and the empty state shown when nothing is selected. |
| labelPosition | "outside" \| "inside" |  | Where every row's label sits: its own column (the default), or inside one box per row, as many design tools do. |
| container | HTMLElement \| null |  | Where pickers and menus are portalled. Defaults to document.body. |
| density | "default" \| "compact" |  | Compact uses 28px filled fields and body-style group titles. The --uicoolkit-field-* CSS variables fine-tune either density. |
| disabled / motion | boolean |  | Disable every field; turn off group and field transitions. Reduced motion is always honored. |
| messages | { label, empty, mixed, multiple, single, add, remove, hide, show, mixedList } |  | Replace the panel's text: its name, the empty state, Mixed, the multiple-selection title, the single-item reason, + and −, a list entry's hide and show names, and the note for lists that differ. |
| usePropertyInspectorProperty() | hook |  | The binding the generic row uses, for building a row of your own around any control. |

## Supported states

- locked

- disabled

## Customization

Pass the host's current selection to `items` and choose which groups and controls to render. Use `onPreview` for ephemeral canvas feedback and `onCommit` to apply the final change once to the affected IDs. `applyPropertyChange` is available for immutable updates. Use the grid for mixed-width cells, list parts for repeatable entries, and custom field bindings for application-specific data. Image rows receive the host's upload callback and image library.

~~~tsx
<PropertyInspector items={selection} onCommit={commit} motion={false} className="max-w-sm rounded-none">
  <PropertyInspectorHeader />
  <PropertyInspectorEmpty />
  <PropertyInspectorGroup title="Spacing" className="border-t border-dashed">
    <PropertyInspectorNumber property="gap" label="Gap" unit="px" min={0} />
  </PropertyInspectorGroup>
</PropertyInspector>
~~~

Use `density="compact"` for dense panels. To match your own fields, set these CSS variables on the inspector or any ancestor: `--uicoolkit-field-height`, `--uicoolkit-field-bg`, `--uicoolkit-field-border`, `--uicoolkit-field-shadow`, `--uicoolkit-field-icon-bg`, `--uicoolkit-field-icon-border` and `--uicoolkit-field-icon-width`. Inner controls follow the field height. Inspector Field, Number Field, Alignment Control, Color Picker and Split Number Field read the same variables when used on their own.

Test an empty selection, matching values, mixed values and edits to a subset of the selection. Keep locked reasons available when supplying custom rows.

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The inspector is a region named “Properties”; the selection title updates politely when the selection changes.

- Groups are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded; collapsed content is inert, so hidden fields are skipped by Tab.

- Every row is an Inspector Field: labels name their controls, and Mixed, locked and unavailable states are announced with their reasons.

- A property made of parts shows Mixed only in the parts that differ, and each part is named with the property, such as “Padding top”.

- In the compact grid a field may show only “X” or an icon, but it is still named in full, such as “Rotation”; one-shot actions form a toolbar with one tab stop.

- An optional group's + and − are named, such as “Add Flex” and “Remove Flex”, with tooltips; a group with no items hides its fields from the tab order.

- Each list entry is a group named such as “Fill 2”, with named hide, show and remove buttons; a hidden entry stays editable. A settings row opens a dialog named after it, and Escape returns focus to the row.

- Numbers can be typed, stepped with the arrow keys or dragged; dragging is never the only way to change a value.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Home screen
 ); } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | name | string | | The screen's committed name. files.content: # Sortable List Reorder rows by dragging a handle or with Move up and Move down. Your app owns the order and gets each finished move once; if saving fails, the list offers to retry. ## Release Version: 0.1.3. Status: experimental. License: MIT. ## Prerequisites Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package. React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported. ## Install Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version: ~~~sh npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/sortable-list/0.1.3.json ~~~ For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs. ## Files and dependencies - @ui/sortable-list-content.tsx - @ui/sortable-list-controls.tsx - @ui/sortable-list-retry.tsx - @ui/sortable-list-root.tsx - @ui/sortable-list-state.tsx - @ui/sortable-list.tsx - @ui/sortable-list.md Npm dependencies: motion@14.6.0. Pinned registry dependencies: none. ## Installed guide This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as sortable-list.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates. ## Minimal working example This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence. ~~~tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { SortableList, SortableListContent, SortableListItem, SortableListHandle, SortableListMoveUp, SortableListMoveDown, SortableListEmpty, SortableListError } from "@/components/ui/sortable-list"; type Item = { id: string; title: string }; export default function SortableListExample() { const [items, setItems] = useState([{ id: "a", title: "Draft" }, { id: "b", title: "Review" }]); return ( item.id} getLabel={item => item.title} onOrderChange={async next => { setItems(next); }}> {(item: Item) => ( {item.title} )} No items yet. ); } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | items | T[] | | Your ordered items. The list shows them in this order and never reorders them itself. | | getId | (item: T) => string \| number | | A stable identity for each item. Never derived from position. | | getLabel | (item: T) => string | | Name used in button labels and announcements, such as a task title. | | onOrderChange | (items: T[], move: { item, from, to }) => void \| Promise | | Called once per completed move. Save it and update items. A returned promise shows saving; rejecting restores your order and offers Retry. | | isLocked | (item: T) => boolean | | Items that cannot be moved; their handle and move buttons are unavailable. | | disabled | boolean | false | Shows the list without allowing moves. | | motion | boolean | true | Layout and lift animation. Reduced motion is always honored. | | messages | { handle, moveUp, moveDown, moved, restored } | | Replace button labels and screen reader announcements, for example to translate them. Each is a function of the item's label (and position). | | SortableListContent | (item, index) => ReactNode | | The list. Its render function returns a SortableListItem for each item. | | Handle, MoveUp, MoveDown | parts | | Drag from the handle (arrows, Home and End also work on it), or move one place with the buttons. Unavailable moves are aria-disabled so focus stays put. | | Empty, Error | parts | | Shown when there are no items, and after a rejected save with a Retry button. | | className | string | | Every part accepts className, merged after defaults so yours win. Rows expose data-dragging and data-locked; the root exposes data-status. | | useSortableList() | hook | | Displayed items, status, failure, move(id, to), retry and dismiss, for building your own parts. | ## Supported states - empty - single - saving - error - disabled ## Styling and replaced content The list is generic over your item type; use stable IDs rather than array positions. Its content render function lets your row contain real icons, metadata and actions. Every part accepts native attributes, className and a forwarded ref. ~~~tsx item.id} getLabel={item => item.title} onOrderChange={persistOrder} motion={false} className="rounded-2xl border p-4"> {(item: Item) => ( {item.title} Earlier Later )} Add a step to get started. ~~~ Use the complete imports and Item type from the minimal example. persistOrder is your application callback. ## State, saving and recovery The app owns items. A drag previews a candidate order and one completed move calls onOrderChange once, with the new list and move information. Await persistence before committing the new items to state. Rejection restores the authoritative order, announces recovery and exposes Retry. Include SortableListError, or provide an equivalent failure surface through useSortableList. Retry reapplies the failed item’s placement relative to the nearest surviving neighbor in the current app order. New rows, current object data, removals and unrelated row ordering are preserved; callback positions describe the current move. Retry is unavailable while disabled or pending, when the moved item is gone or the placement is already applied, or when it would move a locked item. Re-enable/unlock to retry, make a new move, or dismiss the old failure through useSortableList. isLocked keeps an item in its slot. disabled prevents changes to the entire list. Movement controls stay focusable when unavailable. Replace messages to localize handle labels and move/restoration announcements. ~~~tsx item.id} getLabel={item => item.title} onOrderChange={async next => { await api.saveOrder(next.map(item => item.id)); setItems(next); }} messages={{ moveUp: label => "Move " + label + " earlier" }}> {children} ~~~ The api and children in this integration fragment belong to the host app. Do not add artificial success timers to delivered source. ## Motion and boundaries Set motion={false} to turn off optional lift/layout animation. Reduced motion is honored. Drag only from the handle so the rest of the row can scroll and receive actions. Keep move buttons for non-drag operation. One vertical list only. Nested trees, multiple containers, Kanban, virtualization and cross-window dragging are outside this release; use representative real content before adopting it for very large lists. ## Accessibility and integration checks - Every move has a non-drag route: Move up and Move down buttons, plus arrows, Home and End on the handle. - Each completed move is announced once with the item's name and new position; a failed save announces where it returned. - Focus stays on the control you used, even when the row reaches the top or bottom. - Escape during a drag cancels it and keeps the original order. - Dragging starts only from the handle, so touch scrolling on the rest of the row still works. - Layout animation is skipped with reduced motion or motion={false}. # Split Number Field

Edit a value that splits into parts, such as padding into its sides or radius into its corners. Merged parts list values that differ; each part types, steps and drags like a Number Field.

## Release

Version: 0.2.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

## Install

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/split-number-field/0.2.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/split-number-field-presets.tsx

- @ui/split-number-field-root.tsx

- @ui/split-number-field-state.tsx

- @ui/split-number-field.tsx

- @ui/split-number-field.md

Npm dependencies: none beyond the host React/shadcn setup.

Pinned registry dependencies: number-field@0.2.0.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as split-number-field.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { sidesPreset, SplitNumberField, SplitNumberFieldParts, SplitNumberFieldToggle, type SplitNumberValue } from "@/components/ui/split-number-field";

export default function SplitNumberFieldExample() {
  const [padding, setPadding] = useState<SplitNumberValue>({ left: 12, right: 12, top: 8, bottom: 8 });
  return (
    <SplitNumberField label="Padding" preset={sidesPreset} value={padding} onValueCommit={setPadding} unit="px" min={0}>
      <SplitNumberFieldParts />
      <SplitNumberFieldToggle />
    </SplitNumberField>
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| preset | { levels, toggleLabel, toggleIcon } |  | How the value splits. sidesPreset goes horizontal/vertical → four sides (padding, margin); allSidesPreset goes one value → four sides (border width); cornersPreset goes one value → four corners. Define your own levels, labels and icons. |
| value | Record<part, number \| null> |  | Every finest part, such as left, top, right and bottom, even while merged. null is Mixed, for a selection with different values. |
| onValueCommit | (value, { changed }) => void |  | Called once per finished edit with every part and the ones it changed, so a selection can apply only those. |
| Typed lists | "8, 20" |  | A merged part whose sides differ starts editing from its list. Type as many values as it shows to replace each one, as many as it covers to set them in order, or one value for all. |
| onValueChange | (value, { changed }) => void |  | Live values while dragging a part, for previewing on your canvas. |
| level / defaultLevel / onLevelChange | number |  | Which level shows. By default it starts at the first level that hides no difference. |
| align | "start" \| "end" | "start" | Where values sit in each part: after the icon, or at the end beside the unit, as Inspector Field's align. |
| unit / min / max / step / validate / … | Number Field props |  | Passed to every part, so margin can allow negatives and limits reject typed values with a message. |
| SplitNumberFieldParts / Toggle | parts |  | The current level's Number Fields in a two-column grid, and the button that splits or merges them. |
| messages | { mixed, values, part, listCount, listRange } |  | Replace the Mixed text, how differing values are listed, how each part is named and the typed-list messages, for example to translate them. |

## Supported states

- mixed

- disabled

- read-only

## Customization

Use a supplied sides or corners preset, or define the grouped and expanded parts for your own value. Pass a value keyed by the preset's parts. Apply only the keys listed in the commit's `changed` array to multi-selection edits. A differing set of values on one item is distinct from mixed values across items.

~~~tsx
<SplitNumberField label="Radius" preset={cornersPreset} value={radius} onValueCommit={commit} min={0} unit="px" motion={false} className="font-mono">
  <SplitNumberFieldParts />
  <SplitNumberFieldToggle />
</SplitNumberField>
~~~

Check that expansion keeps the intended part names and that editing one part preserves the others.

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The field is a group named by its label; each part is a spin button named with it, such as Padding top.

- Every part can be typed, stepped with the arrow keys (Shift for 10) or dragged; dragging is never the only way.

- A merged part reads its differing values, and they can be edited as a typed list; a list that cannot apply is rejected with a message.

- The toggle is a pressed button named for its preset, such as Individual sides.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

# Stateful Button

Show progress and announce the outcome of an async action. Keep a stable width across labels or animate the button to fit each state.

## Release

Version: 0.1.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/stateful-button/0.1.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/stateful-button.tsx

- @ui/stateful-button.md

Npm dependencies: motion@14.6.0, lucide-react@1.61.0.

Pinned registry dependencies: none.

## Installed guide

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { StatefulButton } from "@/components/ui/stateful-button";

export default function StatefulButtonExample() {
  async function saveSettings() {
    const response = await fetch("/api/settings", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ compact: true }), headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } });
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Save failed");
  }
  return <StatefulButton action={saveSettings} labels={{ idle: "Save settings", success: "Saved" }} />;
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| action | () => Promise<unknown> |  | Resolve to confirm or reject to offer retry. Pending clicks are ignored. |
| status / defaultStatus | ButtonStatus |  | Drive the current state from your app or choose an initial state. |
| widthMode | "stable" \| "animated" | stable | Reserve the widest label and icon, or resize for each state. |
| labels / icons | Partial<Record<ButtonStatus, ReactNode>> |  | Replace state content. Pass null to remove an icon. |
| announcements | Partial<Record<'success' \| 'error', string>> |  | Override the spoken outcome for rich labels or a retry prompt. |
| motion / duration | boolean / number | true / 200 | Enable transitions and set their duration in milliseconds. Reduced motion disables animation. |
| resetAfter | number \| false | 1800 | Milliseconds to keep a successful result. False keeps it until the next action. |
| className | string |  | Styles the native button. Target data-state for state-specific styles. |

## Supported states

- idle

- loading

- success

- error

- disabled

## Integration

Connect the action to your save handler. Resolve after a successful write and reject on failure so the user can retry. The example expects your app to provide /api/settings.

## Customization

Styles the native button. Target data-state for state-specific styles.

```tsx
<StatefulButton
  action={upgradePlan}
  widthMode="animated"
  labels={{ idle: "Upgrade plan", loading: "Upgrading…", success: "Welcome aboard" }}
  className="rounded-full border bg-secondary font-mono text-secondary-foreground"
/>
```

- Enter and Space activate the native button. Loading keeps focus and prevents duplicate submissions.

- A polite status region announces the configured outcome.

- Reduced motion and Motion off stop transitions and the spinner.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

# Upload Dropzone Upload multiple files with a progress row for each. Retry an interrupted file, see why a file was rejected, and add more alongside completed uploads. ## Release Version: 0.1.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT. ## Prerequisites Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package. React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported. ## Install Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version: ~~~sh npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/upload-dropzone/0.1.0.json ~~~ For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs. ## Files and dependencies - @ui/upload-dropzone.tsx - @ui/upload-queue.ts - @ui/upload-row.tsx - @ui/upload-dropzone.md Npm dependencies: lucide-react@1.61.0. Pinned registry dependencies: none. ## Installed guide This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as upload-dropzone.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates. ## Minimal working example This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence. ~~~tsx "use client"; import { UploadDropzone } from "@/components/ui/upload-dropzone"; export default function UploadDropzoneExample() { return { const data = new FormData(); data.append("attachment", file); const response = await fetch("/api/attachments", { method: "POST", body: data, signal }); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Upload failed"); }} />; } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | upload | (file, onProgress, signal) => Promise | | Resolve when stored, reject with an error to enable retry. Report a fraction from 0 to 1 when known. Unmount aborts the signal. | | accept | Record | | Allowed MIME types, wildcards and filename extensions for both the picker and drops. Omit to allow all files. | | maxFiles | number | | Maximum accepted files per selection or drop. Extra files get individual rejection reasons. Earlier rows stay visible. | | hint / disabled / motion | string / boolean / boolean | | Describe restrictions, disable adding and retrying, or stop progress animations. | | className / buttonClassName | string | | Restyle the outer surface and browse button with host tokens. | | renderRow | (entry, retry) => ReactNode | | Compose custom rows with the filename, size, status, progress, message and retry action. | ## Supported states - empty - uploading - error - complete ## Integration Provide an upload function that resolves after the transfer finishes and rejects on failure. Pass the abort signal to your transport. Report fractional progress when the transport provides it. The example expects your app to provide /api/attachments. ## Customization Restyle the outer surface and browse button with host tokens. ```tsx (
{entry.name} · {entry.message ?? entry.status} {entry.status === "failed" && }
)} /> ``` ## Accessibility and integration checks - Browse files and Add more files open the native picker by keyboard. - Progress bars have a filename and numeric value only when the host reports progress. A polite summary announces outcomes. - Each failed upload has a named Retry button. Reduced motion disables bar transitions and pulsing. Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling. ## Updates and conflicts Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/upload-dropzone/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates. If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry. ## License MIT. Dependencies retain their respective licenses.

{version.name}
} /> ); } ~~~ ## API and composition | Part / property | Type | Default | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | versions | { id, name, current?, status? }[] | | The alternatives. status is ready, loading or error. | | compare / onCompareChange | { a, b } / function | | The two version ids being compared. Your app owns them. | | renderVersion | (version, { slot, size }) => ReactNode | | Draws a version for the stage, or as a small thumbnail in the A and B menus. | | changes | { label, before, after }[] | | What differs between A and B. The current version cannot be deleted. | | onRetry | (id) => void | | Offers Retry on a version that failed to load. | | defaultMode | "side" \| "swipe" \| "overlay" | | The starting mode. Phones start on Swipe, other screens on Side by side. | | onDividerChange / onDividerCommit | (position) => void | | Live and finished divider positions from 0 to 1. | | onOpacityChange / onOpacityCommit | (opacity) => void | | Live and finished overlay opacity from 0 to 1. | | aspectRatio | string | "16 / 10" | The shape of the stage and thumbnails. | | container / disabled / messages | HTMLElement / boolean / object | | Choose where menus portal, turn off actions, replace the text. | | VersionComparisonToolbar / Stage / Opacity / Changes / Label | parts | | Compose or reorder the panel. | | useVersionComparison | hook | | The compared versions and view state, for custom parts. | ## Supported states - empty - loading - error - disabled ## Integration Keep the versions and A/B pair in the host. renderVersion receives a stage or thumbnail size so heavy previews can use small static thumbnails in selectors. items.title: XY Pad
items.description: Set two numbers with one draggable point, with a field for each axis.

files.content:
# XY Pad

Set two related numbers with one drag, such as a shadow offset or focal point. Each axis has its own range, and a Number Field for exact values.

## Release

Version: 0.1.0. Status: experimental. License: MIT.

## Prerequisites

Use a TypeScript React app with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn theme tokens and an initialized components.json. The app must already have its shadcn cn utility at the configured utils alias. UICoolKit does not replace that utility or install a required runtime package.

React 18.3/19 consumers are verified in Next.js and Vite using the version pairings documented at https://uicoolkit.com/compatibility.json. React 18 uses a compatible Next.js Pages Router fixture; React 19 uses App Router. Do not infer that every Next.js/React combination is supported.

## Install

Use the item URL returned by the current catalog. This example installs an immutable version:

~~~sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://uicoolkit.com/r/xy-pad/0.1.0.json
~~~

For namespaced use, configure @uicoolkit to https://uicoolkit.com/r/{name}.json in components.json first. Namespace aliases resolve the current release; immutable URLs are preferable for reproducible installs.

## Files and dependencies

- @ui/xy-pad-drag.ts

- @ui/xy-pad-fields.tsx

- @ui/xy-pad-math.ts

- @ui/xy-pad-parts.tsx

- @ui/xy-pad-root.tsx

- @ui/xy-pad-state.tsx

- @ui/xy-pad.tsx

- @ui/xy-pad.md

Npm dependencies: none beyond the host React/shadcn setup.

Pinned registry dependencies: number-field@0.2.0.

## Installed guide

This same version-matched guide installs beside the component at the configured ui alias as xy-pad.md. Read it and the local source before modifying an existing installation. It remains available offline; check current registry metadata only when discovering items or reviewing updates.

## Minimal working example

This example keeps state in the app; it does not imply a backend or durable persistence.

~~~tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { XYPad, type XYPadValue } from "@/components/ui/xy-pad";

export default function XYPadExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<XYPadValue>({ x: 0, y: 0 });
  return (
    <XYPad className="max-w-64 rounded-xl border border-border p-4" label="Shadow offset" value={value}
      xAxis={{ label: "Offset X", min: -24, max: 24, unit: "px" }}
      yAxis={{ label: "Offset Y", min: -24, max: 24, unit: "px" }}
      onValueChange={setValue} onValueCommit={setValue} />
  );
}
~~~

## API and composition

| Part / property | Type | Default | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| value | { x, y } |  | The committed value. An axis can be null for a mixed selection. |
| onValueCommit | (value, detail) => void |  | Called once per finished drag, key press or field edit. detail names the changed axes and the source. |
| onValueChange | (value, detail) => void |  | Live values, and the starting value when a drag is cancelled. |
| xAxis / yAxis | object |  | Each sets label, shortLabel, min, max, step, largeStep, precision and unit. |
| yDirection | "down" \| "up" | "down" | Which way larger Y values run. Use up for charts and spring settings. |
| label | string |  | The pad's name, shown above the surface and read by screen readers. |
| disabled / readOnly / motion / messages | boolean / boolean / boolean / object |  | Turn off or lock editing; turn off the point's press transition; replace the text. |
| XYPadLabel | part |  | The pad's visible name. Place it above the surface. |
| XYPadSurface | part |  | The square area you press and drag. It fills the pad, which is 160 px wide unless you set its width. Defaults to the grid, origin dot and point. |
| XYPadGrid / XYPadOrigin / XYPadThumb | parts |  | Equal grid cells (set cells to change how many, 6 by default), a dot at zero or the middle, and the point. Place them inside the surface. |
| XYPadFields / XYPadField | parts |  | Number Fields for both axes, or one with axis set to x or y. |
| useXYPad | hook |  | The live value, axes and state, for custom parts. |

## Supported states

- mixed

- disabled

## Integration

Supply xAxis and yAxis labels, bounds, steps and units. Use XYPadSurface and XYPadFields separately when the point and the numeric inputs belong in different spaces.

Connect onValueChange to a live preview and onValueCommit to saved state. Supply a controlled value to synchronize another editor with the same two numbers.

## Customization

Use a narrow root for an inspector row or give the surface a different aspect ratio with className. Change the theme primary token to restyle the point.

```tsx
<XYPadSurface className="aspect-video rounded-2xl bg-muted" />
```

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The point is one slider tab stop. Arrow keys change X and Y, Shift takes a larger step, and Home and End go to the X limits.

- Both values are read with the point, and each key press commits once.

- Escape cancels a drag and restores the starting value.

- The pad's border shows keyboard focus, and Number Fields give an exact alternative to dragging.

- The point's short press transition turns off with reduced motion.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

## Updates and conflicts

Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/xy-pad/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates.

If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry.

## License

MIT. Dependencies retain their respective licenses.

| disabled / readOnly / motion / messages | boolean / boolean / boolean / object |  | Turn off or lock editing; turn off the point's press transition; replace the text. |
| XYPadLabel | part |  | The pad's visible name. Place it above the surface. |
| XYPadSurface | part |  | The square area you press and drag. It fills the pad, which is 160 px wide unless you set its width. Defaults to the grid, origin dot and point. |
| XYPadGrid / XYPadOrigin / XYPadThumb | parts |  | Equal grid cells (set cells to change how many, 6 by default), a dot at zero or the middle, and the point. Place them inside the surface. |
| XYPadFields / XYPadField | parts |  | Number Fields for both axes, or one with axis set to x or y. |
| useXYPad | hook |  | The live value, axes and state, for custom parts. |

## Supported states

- mixed

- disabled

## Integration

Supply xAxis and yAxis labels, bounds, steps and units. Use XYPadSurface and XYPadFields separately when the point and the numeric inputs belong in different spaces.

Connect onValueChange to a live preview and onValueCommit to saved state. Supply a controlled value to synchronize another editor with the same two numbers.

## Customization

Use a narrow root for an inspector row or give the surface a different aspect ratio with className. Change the theme primary token to restyle the point.

```tsx
<XYPadSurface className="aspect-video rounded-2xl bg-muted" />
```

## Accessibility and integration checks

- The point is one slider tab stop. Arrow keys change X and Y, Shift takes a larger step, and Home and End go to the X limits.

- Both values are read with the point, and each key press commits once.

- Escape cancels a drag and restores the starting value.

- The pad's border shows keyboard focus, and Number Fields give an exact alternative to dragging.

- The point's short press transition turns off with reduced motion.

Check multiple independent instances, keyboard/focus, touch, both themes, reduced motion, server rendering and your own async failure paths after restyling.

Read the installed version's history at https://uicoolkit.com/r/xy-pad/history.json. Review changelog, compatibility, migration notes and differences against your locally edited files before applying an update. Never silently overwrite existing source or use an overwrite flag without the consumer's explicit decision. There are no automatic source updates.

If setup or dependencies are missing, stop and fix the documented prerequisite before retrying. If a fetch or install fails, inspect what changed, retain the original files and report partial work. Installed source continues working without the registry.
